title: genomic-benchmarks-data Package Metadata
description: Schema for included collection metadata distributed with the genomic-benchmarks-data package. Local dataset_path values are intentionally omitted.

schema_version.description: The version of this schema the document claims to conform to. Pinned with const rather than a pattern so that the number and the shape it names cannot drift apart: changing the schema means changing this value and all seven collection files in one commit, and a file left behind fails validation rather than quietly claiming a version it no longer matches. It is here because a consumer cannot version someone else's schema - genomic-benchmarks-leaderboard pins the versions it understands, so its contract test fails with 'metadata schema moved from 1.0 to 1.1' instead of a KeyError three calls deep. Bump the major when a reader written for the previous major can misread a document: a field removed, renamed or retyped, the meaning of an existing field changed, or a value added to task_type or molecular_level - those two are the fields a consumer switches on, and the leaderboard derives public_metric from task_type. Bump the minor when it cannot: a field added, or a constraint tightened so that only documents which were already wrong begin to fail.

collection.description: Name of the dataset collection (for example: BEACON, GUE_v2, genomic-benchmarks).

collection_doi.description: Primary publication or source DOI for the collection.

licence.description: The collection's licence, and specifically whether its split files may be republished. Required, because publish_datasets.py has to decide whether a split's file may be uploaded or must be left at its original source, and a missing value must fail rather than default. A dataset entry may override it where a collection mixes licences.

datasets.description: List of dataset entries that belong to this collection.

licence.description: A licence, and what it permits. Held at collection level and optionally overridden per dataset, because one collection mixes them: three mRNABench datasets are CC BY 4.0 and the rest are published with no licence stated.

name.description: SPDX-style or common name of the licence, for example CC BY 4.0. Null where the source states none, which is not the same as permissive: an absent licence grants nothing.

url.description: Where the licence text was read from.

redistribution.description: Whether this repository may republish the split files. The one field publish_datasets.py branches on: permitted uploads the file, and denied or unknown leave it to be fetched from its original source, with only dataset_url and sha256 naming it. unknown is kept distinct from denied on purpose - an unanswered licence is not a refusal, and answering one flips a collection over in a single edit.

note.description: Why the redistribution value is what it is - the evidence, not a restatement. A denial should name who declined and when.

stringToStringMap.description: Generic map from string keys to string values.

min.description: Minimum observed label value in the split.

max.description: Maximum observed label value in the split.

median.description: Median observed label value in the split.

seqAlphabet.description: Map from sequence column names to the set of observed symbols in that column.

seqLengthSummary.description: Summary statistics for observed sequence lengths.

min.description: Minimum observed sequence length in the split.

max.description: Maximum observed sequence length in the split.

median.description: Median observed sequence length in the split.

seqLength.description: Map from sequence column names to length summaries for that column.

classRatio.description: Class distribution for classification tasks. TODO: confirm whether values are exact proportions or rounded summaries.

labelsField.description: Label metadata for a split: either categorical labels (array) or numeric summary (object).

splitMetadataEntry.description: Metadata for one split (for example train/val/test).

seq_length.description: Observed length summary for each sequence input column, if available.

seq_alphabet.description: Observed alphabet for each sequence input column.

labels.description: Label values or label summary for this split.

dataset_size.description: Number of rows/examples in this split.

class_ratio.description: Class proportions for this split, if applicable to the task.

all_columns.description: All columns present in the released split file, including the id and row_index columns when materialised by the publisher.

dataset_url.description: Download URL for the split dataset file.

sha256.description: SHA256 checksum of the split dataset file used to verify file integrity.

splitMetadata.description: Mapping from split name (for example train, val, test) to split-specific metadata.

datasetEntry.description: Metadata for one included dataset/task within the collection. Excluded source datasets are omitted from this package.

core_set.description: Whether this dataset belongs to the benchmark core set.

major_version.description: The major version of this dataset's data - not of the schema, which is schema_version, and not a version of this document. It is the third field of every sequence ID in the dataset (<collection>:<dataset>:<major version>:<split>:<index>) and the path prefix its published files sit under, so it is the one part of an identity that says whether a result computed last year still refers to the same sequences. Written by the collection's curation notebook from DEFAULT_MAJOR_VERSION in curation/utils.py, the same constant write_split stamps into the IDs it mints, so this field and the files cannot claim different versions of the same rows. Recorded here because a consumer cannot otherwise learn it for every split: one this project may republish carries its IDs in the file and can be asked, but one whose licence bars re-upload is served by its original source without them and has its index composed from row order. Bumped when a dataset's sequences change: indices restart at zero, the files move to a new prefix rather than being rewritten in place, and every previously published result keeps naming the old version.

task_description.description: Human-readable summary of the prediction task.

species.description: Species covered by the dataset. Multiple species may be encoded as a pipe-separated string. TODO: confirm canonical encoding for multi-species metadata.

task_type.description: Task type, from a closed vocabulary in sentence case. Enumerated because it was not: two collections wrote Title Case, which split Binary classification into two task types and cost 20 of the 75 binary datasets to anyone grouping on the raw string. A genuinely new task type is added here first, deliberately, as for molecular_level.

seq_col.description: Sequence input column name(s) used by the task.

label_col.description: Label column name(s) in the dataset file(s).

label_categories.description: Map from label ID/key to class description. Null for non-categorical tasks. A retained dataset whose task_type contains 'classification' must carry at least two entries - see the conditional below. Nothing enforced it before, and one of the 75 binary datasets was null while its nine siblings were not.

splits.description: Available split names for this dataset entry.

task_category.description: High-level biological or benchmark task category.

molecular_level.description: Molecular level represented by the dataset.

positive_label.description: Label value treated as the positive class for scoring, or null when the task has no positive class.

scoring_splits.description: Split names used for benchmark scoring, or null when the dataset is not scored.

scoring_metric.description: Metric used for benchmark scoring, or null when no scoring metric is specified.

dataset_doi.description: Primary publication or source DOI for the dataset in the collection.

licence.description: This dataset's licence, where it differs from its collection's. Present only as an override; absent means the collection's applies.
